## Context / Problem

The on-box MCP container keeps 1.2-2.3 GB of anonymous memory for hours after gate jobs finish, with no request in flight. On 2026-10-28 that plateau sat at 3.2-3.4 GB for 2 h 12 min before a burst of concurrent reads pushed it over the 3.63 GiB limit and the kernel OOM-killed the server (teenage-unquieted-ringworm). It still happens on current main.

## Observation

- 2026-10-28: 0.93 GB -> 3.28 GB between 15:29 and 15:34 PDT with only `PingRequest` in the log; OOM kill at 17:47 PDT.
- 2026-11-16, deployed `b4e0d01b649` (`rebar-mcp-b4e0d01b6491-8092`, read-only SSM): last gate activity 19:44:14 UTC (plan-review jobs, `GATE_PEAK_RSS` up to 1.47 GB). Samples at 19:47, 19:52, 19:57, 20:02, 20:07 and 20:11 UTC all read cgroup `anon=1273MB`, process `RssAnon=1273MB`, 4 threads, 0 `CallToolRequest` in the prior 5 min. Before the gates (15:38-18:55 UTC) the same container idled at 342 MB.
- The holder is PID 1, `/app/.venv/bin/rebar-mcp`, the only process in the container; its `RssAnon` equals the cgroup `anon` figure.
- `/proc/1/smaps` while idle: 703 MB of RSS sits in 11 glibc per-thread arena heaps (64 MB VMAs), 547 MB in other anonymous mappings, 22 MB in the main `[heap]`.
- Store-wide reads return their memory (6 concurrent `list_tickets`/`ready`/`summary` in the MCP image: peak 656 MB, 71 MB idle after).

## Root cause (reproduced)

A gate runs on a worker thread (`spawn_context_daemon`, `src/rebar/_opcert_binding.py:101`; AnyIO workers for the sync tools). Its large strings (prompts, tool output; anything over 512 bytes bypasses pymalloc) come from that thread's glibc arena. When they are freed, glibc keeps the pages in the arena because a few small surviving allocations pin it, and nothing ever calls `malloc_trim`. Reproduced in `python:3.12-slim` (the MCP base image): a gate-shaped worker thread that builds and drops ~1 GB of strings while keeping 1,200 small results leaves RssAnon at 983 MB idle with 970 MB reported free by `mallinfo2`; `malloc_trim(0)` brings it to 24 MB in 70 ms.

## Approach

Return freed C-heap pages to the OS whenever the server goes idle. The in-flight gauge (`InFlightGauge`, `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:75`) already counts every certified/signing tool call (`admit`, line 122; `track`, line 149), every daemon spawned while serving (`serving_gauge` -> `tracked_work(gauge.hold)`, line 221; `spawn_context_daemon` takes the hold at `_opcert_binding.py:124`), the boot sweep (line 381) and each idle-sync tick (line 437). All of them release through `InFlightGauge._releaser` (line 136). When a release takes the count to zero, call a new `release_freed_heap()` that invokes glibc `malloc_trim(0)` through `ctypes`, outside the gauge lock. Where the C library has no `malloc_trim` (macOS, musl) it is a no-op returning `False`. No config key, environment variable or flag: the behaviour is unconditional, and `malloc_trim(0)` only releases free pages, never live objects.

Rejected: `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` in `Dockerfile.mcp` (adds an environment knob and only narrows fragmentation); switching allocator (new dependency).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`: add `_malloc_trim()` (cached `ctypes` lookup) and `release_freed_heap()`; `_releaser` calls it when the count reaches zero.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py` (new): gauge-trigger tests plus a Linux memory test.

## Testing

- Trim fires only on the release that takes the gauge to zero (two holders: none after the first release, one after the second, none on a repeated release); a tracked certified call trims on exit; an uncounted tool (`show_ticket`) never trims.
- `release_freed_heap()` returns `True` on Linux and `False` elsewhere.
- Linux only: a counted worker thread builds and drops ~250 MB of strings while keeping 240 small objects; after the last release, `RssAnon` must be within 64 MiB of the baseline. Measured in the MCP base image: passes with the change; with the trim call removed it fails ("idle process kept 252 MiB").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The process or thread holding the memory during a plateau is identified with evidence and recorded here: PID 1 `rebar-mcp`, glibc per-thread arenas (Observation above). Evidence: read-only SSM smaps 2026-11-16 (703 MB of 1,273 MB idle anon in 11 thread-arena heaps).
- [x] The holder releases its memory when its work ends: `InFlightGauge._releaser` calls `release_freed_heap()` when the count reaches zero, and `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py` passes. Landed in Gerrit change 3407, merged as 9beecb409ab.
- [x] A test fails if a finished background job keeps its memory: `test_finished_background_job_does_not_keep_its_memory` fails with the trim call removed and passes with it (Linux, CI `ubuntu-latest`). Measured in the MCP base image: without the trim "idle process kept 252 MiB", with it 4 passed; CI Verified +1 on change 3407.
- [x] `make verify` passes, and `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0. Local run: lint (including the mechanism ratchet, exit 0), typecheck and import guard passed; default tier 21,285 passed, and its 6 failures (sandbox PermissionError on AF_UNIX/forkserver, 5 s `git rev-parse` timeouts at load ~60, one crashed worker) all passed on rerun outside the sandbox; integration tier 218 passed. CI Verified +1 on change 3407.
- [x] After the change deploys, an idle sample of the live MCP container at least 10 minutes after its last gate job is recorded on this ticket (cgroup `anon` and `/proc/1` `RssAnon`), with the share of memory still held in glibc thread arenas. `rebar-mcp-9beecb409abb-8093`, 00:59 UTC 2026-11-17, 730 s after the last of 3 plan-review gates: anon 328 MB, RssAnon 328 MB, glibc thread arenas 21 MB (old code: 1,273 MB / 703 MB). Remainder tracked in waxy-nonspheral-cutworm.
